objects.frozen: Actual centered Gaussian target laws pi_A and their actual Haar-mixture single-block laws P_+1/P_-1 and actual averaged ambient laws bar_pi_+1/bar_pi_-1. The density symbols p_b and bar_p_b refer to those laws, not freely supplied nonnegative functions. The scalar a is the single-block Hellinger affinity from Ex68.

domains.frozen: O_j belongs to real O(n). Single-block sample x_j belongs to Euclidean R^n. Full sample belongs to Euclidean R^d, identified with k ordered blocks and, only if kn<d, one residual Euclidean R^(d-kn) coordinate. All displayed dx integrations are Euclidean Lebesgue integrations in the corresponding dimension.
domains.guard: A coordinate-product model must be connected to the original ambient space with the correct measure transport; abstract product probability measure integration alone does not yet identify the displayed ambient dx.

quantifiers.frozen: Under the fixed hard-family parameters, each sign b in {-1,+1} gives its own mixture law using independent O_1,...,O_k with the same sign b. Ex70 holds for each b. Ex71 compares the plus and minus averaged target laws and asserts one identity for every admissible parameter choice. It does not average independent random signs block by block.

assumptions.frozen: Source standing hard-family conditions are kappa>=4, integers 3<=n<=d, and k=floor(d/n), with O_j sampled independently from the conditioned Haar probability for a fixed b. Consequently k>=1 and 0<=d-kn<n. The identities p_b density of P_b and bar_p_b density of bar_pi_b are source object semantics, not new convenience hypotheses. Source invokes nonnegativity/measurability for Tonelli and normalized residual Gaussian density.
assumptions.binder_guard: Do not insert public premises asserting the conclusion's factorization, actual-law probability/absolute continuity, finite density values, density normalization, or RN identification merely because the implementation needs them. Required proof facts must be derived internally from the actual source constructions, with typing/convention adapters distinguished from genuine source assumptions.

conclusion.frozen: Integral over R^d of sqrt(bar_p_+1(x)*bar_p_-1(x)) dx equals the k-fold product of the single-block affinity integral and, in the kn<d branch, the residual Gaussian integral; hence it equals a^k. Both sides denote affinities of the actual Gaussian mixture laws.
conclusion.formula: int_(R^d) sqrt(bar_p_+(x) bar_p_-(x)) dx = (int_(R^n) sqrt(p_+(y) p_-(y)) dy)^k = a^k
conclusion.guard: A generic theorem about arbitrarily selected tensor-product density functions may serve as a provider but is not itself the source anchor unless actual-law and ambient-Lebesgue identifications are supplied.

scopes_senses.frozen: This is unsquared Hellinger affinity with sqrt(pq), with no 1/2 coefficient and no conversion to Hellinger distance. The residual factor is the same standard Gaussian for both signs and therefore contributes integral phi=1. Independence is within each fixed-sign prior, and the common-sign comparison remains between two different mixture laws.
scopes_senses.representative_guard: The source calls p and bar_p densities and writes a factorized representative. Changing to a.e.-equal density representatives preserves affinity only after a typed a.e. and integration bridge. An arbitrary totalized RN accessor returning zero outside its validity conditions cannot be assumed to denote the actual source density.

constant_dependencies.frozen: The exact tensorization identity contains no exponential constants or dimension-free numerical estimate. Its multiplicity is exactly k=floor(d/n). The residual dimension is d-kn. Kappa affects the actual component laws through Eq4 but introduces no extra multiplicative factor in Ex71. Constants 1/8 and 10 in Eq25/Ex72 do not belong to this identity's proof input.

author_proof_steps.content: Construct the actual single-block and ambient Gaussian mixtures with independent blocks conditional on one common determinant sign.
Identify the actual averaged target with P_b tensor k and the common residual Gaussian; omit residual when kn=d.
Name genuine component densities and set a equal to their single-block Lebesgue affinity.
From Eq6 obtain the full density as product of k copies of p_b times phi_(d-kn) when kn<d.
Use nonnegative density products to split sqrt(bar_p_+ bar_p_-) and apply Tonelli to the resulting nonnegative block factors.
The common residual Gaussian contributes integral phi=1, each identical block factor contributes a, and the finite product is a^k.
For kn=d use the same block calculation with residual coordinate, Gaussian density and Gaussian integral omitted.

conditional_discharge_expectations.discharge: k=floor(d/n), n>=3 and n<=d from S3.SS1.p1.1; may not become an independent convenience premise on top of the fixed source family
p3.1 explicitly introduces phi_(d-kn) only in this branch; Eq70 and the residual Gaussian integral must retain this guard
S3.SS1.p3.2 and p3.3 explicitly omit the residual Gaussian; a zero-dimensional realization is acceptable only with an explicit bridge establishing equivalence to omission
Measurable nonnegative genuine densities and measurable nonnegative square-root products; finite product measure/coordinate transport and sigma-finiteness when used must be supplied internally

Positive-definite Gaussian component construction and mixture integration must establish probability and absolute continuity; source p_b and bar_p_b naming is not permission to assume an unrelated RN accessor is valid

Density normalization and probability yield finite affinity; if an extended-nonnegative integral is used first, conversion to the real source integral must be justified, including finite a.e. RN values when taking toReal
